description: Le présent marché a pour objet de confier à un prestataire unique une mission globale de production de l’édition 2027 du Grand Dîner du Louvre, qui se tiendra le mardi 2 mars 2027 avec environ 450 invités. title: Warehousing Support for CRSP
description: See attached Solicitation. Here is the PWS: Performance Work Statement (PWS): Centralized Receiving and Shipping Point (CRSP) The contractor shall provide Two (2) appropriately trained, supply and services labor to establish, operate, perform, and manage centralized receiving and shipping point (CRSP). Work hours are 0700 1530, Monday through Friday (30min lunch alternating). CRSP tasks include issuing to personnel authorized by delegation of authority card, DA Form 1687 (electronic or manual form acceptable) maintained on file, receiving, unloading or diverting trucks, reviewing manifests, breaking out items, inspecting items, recording transactions, receiving push shipments, redirecting mis-shipments, inspecting, photographing and coordinating with the Installation Transportation Division (ITD). The contractor shall operate the Automated Manifest System (AMS). The contractor shall perform these functions in accordance with AR 710-2, DA PAM 710-2-2 AR 735-5. The contractor shall use material handling, motor transportation to distribute cargo to, or receive cargo from, other CRSPs, ports operations areas, or bases/camps in support of onward movement and retrograde. The contractor shall distribute and backhaul supplies and materials to supply activities on the installation. The contractor shall maintain complete visibility of all ISO containers moving to and from the CRSP and provide input to the Army Container Asset Management System (ACAMS). The contractor shall provide monthly Labor Hours worked per Attachment 0002 Hours Work Report. The contractor shall submit documents per the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) found in Attachments 0003 and 0004. Please note the contractor's Safety and Health Plan (CDRL 002) and Emergency Response Plan (CDRL 003) is due not later than (NLT) 60 days after contract award.

title: VA Magnetic Resonance Safety Expert Services
description: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Midwest Consortium (MIDCON) has a need for contracted Magnetic Resonance Safety Expert (MRSE) virtual coverage. The contractor shall provide virtual support for participating sites for MRSE assistance and guidance in the MIDCON area, Veterans Integrated Services network (VISNs 15 and 23). The contractor shall provide non-personal, non-inherently governmental services in support of magnetic resonance safety at an all-inclusive price. Contractor and contractor personnel shall not be designated as government officials nor make any inherent governmental decisions. Contractor personnel may not supervise or otherwise direct Government employees. The contractor shall support all participating sites in their Magnetic Resonance Safety needs. A comprehensive list of actual requirements will be included in the Performance Work Statement and within the solicitation package document. The period of performance for this requirement consists of five (5) one (1) year ordering periods. The NAICS code for this procurement is 541690, Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services and the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for this requirement is 19 Millon. The proposed requirement action is being set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs). Any vendor desiring to be considered for award MUST also be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) using NAICS code 541690 or a NAICS code with an equivalent size standard. No award can be made unless the vendor is registered in SAM. For additional information and to register in SAM, please access the following web site: www.sam.gov. In order to register with the SAM and to be eligible to receive an award from this acquisition office, all offerors must also have a Unique Entity ID Number. This procurement also requires offerors to complete the electronic representations and certifications at the SAM website. The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contract. Solicitation documents will be made available for download on or about September 11th, 2026 at https://beta.sam.gov. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be issued. Each potential quoter is responsible for checking the website to gain all current information related to the solicitation. The solicitation and any further announcements regarding the solicitation will be posted only at https://beta.sam.gov. The date proposals are due will be stated within the solicitation documents and will be adjusted based upon the actual release date of the solicitation.

title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
description: The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. Applicable standards identified in the Government's technical documentation include, as applicable: USAF Technical Order 35E1-2-13-1 NFPA 54 NFPA 58 NFPA 70 NFPA 1003 NFPA 1402

title: Warehousing Support for CRSP
description: See attached Solicitation. Here is the PWS: Performance Work Statement (PWS): Centralized Receiving and Shipping Point (CRSP) The contractor shall provide Two (2) appropriately trained, supply and services labor to establish, operate, perform, and manage centralized receiving and shipping point (CRSP). Work hours are 0700 1530, Monday through Friday (30min lunch alternating). CRSP tasks include issuing to personnel authorized by delegation of authority card, DA Form 1687 (electronic or manual form acceptable) maintained on file, receiving, unloading or diverting trucks, reviewing manifests, breaking out items, inspecting items, recording transactions, receiving push shipments, redirecting mis-shipments, inspecting, photographing and coordinating with the Installation Transportation Division (ITD). The contractor shall operate the Automated Manifest System (AMS). The contractor shall perform these functions in accordance with AR 710-2, DA PAM 710-2-2 AR 735-5. The contractor shall use material handling, motor transportation to distribute cargo to, or receive cargo from, other CRSPs, ports operations areas, or bases/camps in support of onward movement and retrograde. The contractor shall distribute and backhaul supplies and materials to supply activities on the installation. The contractor shall maintain complete visibility of all ISO containers moving to and from the CRSP and provide input to the Army Container Asset Management System (ACAMS). The contractor shall provide monthly Labor Hours worked per Attachment 0002 Hours Work Report. The contractor shall submit documents per the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) found in Attachments 0003 and 0004. Please note the contractor's Safety and Health Plan (CDRL 002) and Emergency Response Plan (CDRL 003) is due not later than (NLT) 60 days after contract award.

The contractor shall use material handling, motor transportation to distribute cargo to, or receive cargo from, other CRSPs, ports operations areas, or bases/camps in support of onward movement and retrograde. The contractor shall distribute and backhaul supplies and materials to supply activities on the installation. The contractor shall maintain complete visibility of all ISO containers moving to and from the CRSP and provide input to the Army Container Asset Management System (ACAMS). The contractor shall provide monthly Labor Hours worked per Attachment 0002 Hours Work Report. The contractor shall submit documents per the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) found in Attachments 0003 and 0004. Please note the contractor's Safety and Health Plan (CDRL 002) and Emergency Response Plan (CDRL 003) is due not later than (NLT) 60 days after contract award.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS AND SOLICITATION REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) 47QACA26R0306: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 47QACA26R0306 is issued as a request for proposal (RFP), for The Small Business Administration (SBA), the Office of Capital Access (OCA), Office of Credit Risk Management (OCRM), is seeking for a single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract to obtain non-personal services. The contract is for a base year and four option years. Task Orders will be issued on a labor-hours (LH) basis using the Contractor�s fully loaded labor-hour rates, applicable labor categories, and required level of effort. This is a 100% set-aside restricted to responsible SBA-certified Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) participating in the WOSB Federal Contract Program. Offerors must be currently certified as WOSBs in the SBA WOSB certification system at the time of proposal submission and at the time of award. (ii) Please see Attachment A SF 1449 and Attachment B pricing sheet of the solicitation for the list of contract line item(s) and estimated quantities (including option(s) for this requirement). (iii) The Contractor shall provide personnel with the ability to augment the SBA's workforce and support OCRM at its Headquarters office in Washington, D.C. Personnel provided shall support OCRM's activities, to include but not limited to: Delegated Authority Management: Collection, inspection, analysis for delegated authority renewals, nominations, add-ons and re-delegations -Risk Diagnostics: Execution of Desktop Reviews, comprehensive financial analysis and diagnostic activities to assess 7(a) Lender risk. Operational Systems Proficiency: Utilization of federal systems, specifically the Lender Portal and the Capital Access Financial System (CAFS). Preparation of Internal Correspondence: Preparation of data, reports, and correspondence for internal and external stakeholders. Provide assistance with 7(a) loan transfers, invoice resolution, and maintenance of risk identification protocols generation of deliverables to identify SBA Lenders that are, or should be, subject to increased supervision and/or enforcement actions (iv) The anticipated period of performance is October 6, 2026 through October 5, 2027 (not including the four (4) one-year option periods). The Risk Management Support Services will be provided at the location: Small Business Administration Headquarters 409 3rd St. SW Washington, DC 20416 (v) The solicitation and incorporated provisions are those in effect the date of posting and are provided in Section I and K. The full text of provisions may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide. If your firm is interested in this acquisition, you may participate by submitting your response in accordance with the requirements and instructions contained herein. The Government is not liable for any expenses incurred by the offeror in developing and submitting proposals for this RFP. (vi) Offerors shall submit all technical questions concerning this request for proposal in writing by e-mail to bertha.russell@gsa.gov. All questions must be submitted via email and received no later than 9 am Eastern Standard Time on September 14, 2026. Answers will be provided in the form of an amendment and posted in SAM.gov for all vendors to view. (vii) Offers are due no later than 9 a.m. Eastern Standard Time on September 21, 2026. The Government reserves the right to not accept proposals received after the closing date and time. It is the responsibility of the offeror to provide a timely submission and ensure successful delivery to the Government. Required technical and price proposal volumes must be submitted via e-mail directly to Bertha.russell@gsa.gov

title: Acquisition for 10X Genomics GEN X Epi Multiome
description: This requirement is for the procurement of proprietary genomics consumables manufactured by 10x Genomics, Inc., including the GEM-X Epi Multiome system and associated kits. The items to be acquired consist of the GEM-X Epi Multiome, 16 samples (Catalog #1000979), GEM-X Epi Multiome Chip Kit, 4 chips (Catalog #1000951), Single Index Kit N Set A (Catalog #1000212), and 10x Magnetic Separator B (1000394). These products are designed specifically for use with 10x Genomics platforms and are required to support multiomic sequencing workflows. The required products must possess specific functional and performance characteristics to meet the Government�s needs. The consumables and associated equipment must be fully compatible with existing 10x Genomics instrumentation and workflows and enable simultaneous epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling from the same biological sample. The system must support high-throughput processing of up to 16 samples per kit and utilize proprietary reagents that ensure data quality and reproducibility. Additionally, the consumables must be single-use, as required by the manufacturer, and designed to integrate seamlessly with existing laboratory protocols without modification. The magnetic separation equipment must be specifically designed for use with 10x Genomics workflows and enable efficient and reliable bead-based separation steps required in the protocol. These characteristics are essential to maintain continuity of ongoing research and ensure accurate and reliable experimental results.

title: CJAG Fence Install
description: Amendment 1 - 10 Sep 2026 - Add POC for site visit, Added drawing, Added Q&A. Site Visits Encouraged - Call to schedule - Call 1SG Brian Persing 614-336-6975 or CW2 Grant Stoner 614-336-6580. Attachment added: 01_SHEETS-FENCE-V3.pdf Q&A Question 1. Gate Configuration: PWS Paragraph 5.1 identifies two 20-foot manual sliding security gates, while Paragraph 5.1.5 references �swing clearance.� Please confirm whether the required gates are manual sliding gates, swing gates, or another configuration. Answer 1. Manual sliding gates Question 2. Field Measurements / Site Access: The PWS requires the contractor to verify all measurements prior to submitting a quotation. Will the Government conduct a scheduled site visit or otherwise provide access to Load Line 6 for prospective contractors to perform the required field verification before the quotation due date? Answer 2. Can either have a scheduled site visit day or be available when needed by appointment with prospective contactors, although until clearing is complete not much to see. Question 3. Fence Alignment / Drawings: Are drawings, site plans, maps, or other documents available identifying the exact proposed fence alignment and locations of the two 20-foot gates? Answer 3. Fence Alignment drawing was provided (also see attached here, once clearing is complete, BDE 12T assets will be used to layout alignment. Question 4. Completion Schedule: The PWS states a six-month period of performance from contract award; however, the solicitation instructions require a proposed schedule demonstrating completion prior to December 1, 2026. Please confirm whether December 1, 2026 is the mandatory completion deadline or whether the contractor will receive six months from the date of award. Answer 4. Complete prior to December 1 is preferred, also cant start until after clearing is complete in late September / October Question 5. Underground Utilities: The PWS directs the contractor to coordinate with CJAG Department of Public Works to locate and mark underground utilities. Will CJAG/DPW perform the utility locating and marking at no cost to the contractor, or should the contractor include any associated utility-locate costs in its quotation? Answer 5. no active utilities in the area Question 6. Permits: Are any local, state, installation, excavation, or construction permits required for this project? If so, please identify which permits the contractor is responsible for obtaining and paying for. Answer 5. This project is covered under the C-JAG Storm Water Construction Permit and the contractor will have to attend a brief training on the SWP3, submit a co-permittee NOI, sign a Contractor certification form, install additional sediment and erosion controls if necessary, comply with fueling requirements and spill kits, comply with concrete outwash, level ruts, prepare seed bed, and seed and straw all bare earth areas they create. Question 7. Site Conditions / Clearing: Can the Government provide additional information or photographs showing the existing conditions along the approximately 3,850-linear-foot fence alignment, particularly the amount of brush, vegetation, grading, or other site preparation anticipated within the required 10-foot-wide clearing corridor? Answer 7. A site visit is authorized Question 8. Excess Soil / Disposal: May excess soil generated from the post-hole excavation be spread or relocated on Government property at a location designated by the COR, or must all excess soil be removed from Camp James A. Garfield and disposed of off-site? Answer 8. Soil can be spread in the clear zone and a seed bed prepared and all bare earth areas seeded with a C-JAG approved turf grass mix and mulched with 2� to 3� of straw cover. Question 9. Installation Access: Is there an anticipated processing timeframe for contractor and subcontractor personnel to obtain installation access/background-check approval? Additionally, are there any vehicle, equipment, escort, or badging requirements bidders should account for when developing their pricing and schedule? Answer 9. An access roster will be provided, valid drivers license or photo ID must be present at all times. Question 10. Wage Requirements: Please confirm whether a Davis-Bacon Act wage determination or any other prevailing-wage requirement applies to this construction requirement. If applicable, please provide or identify the applicable wage determination. Answer 10. Yes Davis-Bacon Act applies. Question 11. Gate Hardware: Please confirm whether there are any specific requirements for gate latches, locking hardware, rollers/tracks, stops, drop rods, or other gate hardware beyond the requirements currently contained in the PWS and applicable UFS/UFC criteria. Answer 11. There are no additional hardware requirements besides those contained in the PWS and UFS. Question 12. Government-Furnished Information: Are there any additional drawings, specifications, site photographs, utility information, or technical documents that will be provided by amendment before quotations are due? Answer 12. No Question 13. What is the Height of the fence? Answer 13. The fence height is 8 feet, with a minimum of 7 feet of fabric plus the top guard outrigger and barbed wire. Question 14. Is the contractor to install a slide gate or swing gate? Answer 14. Slide Gate Question 15. Are the fence and footers to be removed by installation contractor? Answer 15. Old fence will be removed prior to start of work. Question 16. Can the footers and fence be left on site? Answer 16. No Question 17. Does the fence need to be grounded? If so, how often does it need to be grounded? Answer 17. Grounding is not required for this project. Question 18. What your spec on FE-6, we want to make sure we don�t have tension wire, rods, barbed wire on the inside and outside ect. Answer 18. Not sure what the question is. Question 19. Confirm which specific portions of the project require integrated intrusion detection systems (sensored) versus standard perimeter fencing (non-sensored) to select the correct detail (FEN-03 vs. FEN-04). Answer 19. There will be no intrusion detection systems on the fence. Question 20. Review Hardware: High-security specifications (ASTM F626) mandate specific fittings, tension bands, and tie wires. Ensure your material take-off accounts for these high-security grade accessories rather than standard commercial hardware. Answer 20. Not high security specs Question 21. Confirm Gate Requirements: Refer to the FEN-09 detail specifically for any swing or cantilever gates, as these have distinct framing, post size (often 4-inch or 6 5/8-inch OD depending on width), and bracing requirements compared to the main fence line. Answer 21. Manual sliding gates ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Construction of approximately 3,850 linear feet of FE-6 security fencing, including two 20-foot manual security gates, at Load Line 6, Camp James A. Garfield, Ravenna, Ohio Site visits are encouraged - call 1SG Brian Persing 330-984-8130 or CW2 Grant Stoner 614-336-6580. Only contact for site visits, all other questions are submitted to barry.b.beale.civ@army.mil

title: Vanquish Neo System and Ion Chromatography system
description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is soliciting quotations for the acquisition of two laboratory chromatography systems under one award: Thermo Scientific Vanquish Neo System or Equal for the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM), including all components and accessories necessary to provide a complete and functional system, a twelve (12) month warranty, and two (2) days of on-site LC support. The system must be compatible with the Government-owned Thermo Fisher Scientific Orbitrap Exploris 240 mass spectrometer and associated ion-source/interface configuration. Thermo Scientific Dionex ICS-6000 HPIC System or Equal for the FDA National Forensic Chemistry Center (NFCC), including all required components, supplies, accessories, installation/start-up, and on-site analyst familiarization/training. The Vanquish Neo System will be delivered to Laurel, Maryland, and the Ion Chromatography System will be delivered to Cincinnati, Ohio. Each system is subject to the delivery, warranty, technical, and performance requirements identified in the applicable solicitation attachment. This acquisition is unrestricted and is not set aside for small business concerns. The applicable NAICS code is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. Award will be made using a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) approach. Offerors must provide sufficient technical documentation to demonstrate compliance with all applicable minimum requirements and salient characteristics for both systems. Offerors shall provide itemized pricing for all CLINs and identify the manufacturer, make/model, part number(s), country of origin, and place of manufacture for each proposed end product. Please refer to Solicitation 75F40126Q00430 and its attachments for the complete requirements, quotation instructions, and applicable terms and conditions.

Erosion protection work at the Chilliwack Hatchery, British Columbia for Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO)
description: Erosion protection work at the Chilliwack Hatchery, British Columbia for Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) The work will be conducted at Chilliwack River Hatchery, 55205 Chilliwack Lake Road Chilliwack, BC V4Z 1A7 Riverbank Stabilization and Log Jam removal. Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) requires urgent erosion protection works at the Chilliwack River Hatchery intake area to protect critical infrastructure, including the intake access road, intake pipeline, intake pond, and associated hatchery facilities. Recent riverbank erosion has resulted in significant loss of bank protection within the identified upstream and downstream repair areas. Continued erosion during future high-flow events may result in damage to the access road, exposure of the intake pipeline, and potential failure of the downstream road embankment. The Contractor must provide all labour, equipment, materials, and incidentals necessary to complete the work.

title: Netherlands – Polythene waste and refuse sacks and bags – PMD- en luierzakken 2027 ev voor 12 gemeenten
description: Bizob besteedt aan namens de gemeenten Bergeijk, Bladel, Cranendonck, Eersel, Maashorst, Meierijstad, Oirschot, Reusel-de Mierden, Veldhoven, Vught en werkorganisatie MijnGemeenteDichtbij. De overeenkomst bestaat uit de levering van inzamelzakken van 100% gerecycled LDPE voor: Plastic, Metaal, Drankenkartons (PMD) / Plastic, Blik en Drinkkarton (PBD). In het aanbestedingsdocument spreken we overwegend van PMD. Luiers en incontinentiemateriaal, in het aanbestedingsdocument aangeduid als: luierzak-ken. De opdracht betreft een samengevoegde opdracht, in zowel geografisch opzicht (clustering van gemeenten) als op productniveau (PMD-inzamelzakken en luierzakken). Het samenvoegen in geografisch opzicht zorgt voor een zo groot mogelijk volume van het in grote mate gestandaardiseerd product. Een groot volume heeft een positieve invloed op de prijs. Daarnaast kan er door de gezamenlijke aanpak centraal contractmanagement worden uitgevoerd. Door het samenvoegen is de opdracht voor meerdere partijen interessant en de afleverafstanden zijn beperkt, omdat bestellingen gecombineerd uitgeleverd kunnen worden. In deze markt zijn hoofdzakelijk grote spelers werkzaam. Om de opdracht ook toegankelijk te maken voor het MKB is deze verdeeld in percelen. De opdracht wordt onderverdeeld in de volgende percelen: - Perceel 1: PMD-zakken (geel) - Perceel 2: Luierzakken - Perceel 3: PBD-zakken (oranje) Per perceel wordt er per gemeente met één opdrachtnemer een overeenkomst aangegaan. De overeenkomst wordt aangegaan voor een periode van minimaal twee jaar en maximaal zes jaar. De ingangsdatum van de overeenkomsten is: 1 maart 2027

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. title: USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM and Technical Services
description: This solicitation is for commercial items and has been prepared in accordance with the format outlined in FAR Subpart 12.6, supplemented with additional information contained in this notice. This announcement constitutes the sole solicitation; quotes are hereby requested. Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N40027-26-R-0008 is issues as a FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION solicitation and is being processed under FAR Part 13 � Simplified Acquisition Procedures and FAR Part 6- Competition Requirements. The applicable North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code is 325510 � Paint and Coating Manufacturing. Scope of Requirements The Government seeks sources that can provide support as follows: Product Provision: Provide paint, coatings, and preservation products per the Government's Work Statement. Navy Paint Warranty: Paint, coatings, and preservation products must meet the required standards per the attached Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3). No Waivers/Subcontracts: The responding vendor must provide the required warranty directly, without waiver or subcontracting. OEM Certification: Offerors must provide proof of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certification for the paint and coating systems. Qualified Personnel: Provide Field Service Technical Representatives (FSTR) that meet or exceed the minimum qualifications within the Work Statement in order to perform, inspect, and certify the work stated. Personnel may not be substituted without express written approval by the Government. Hull Coating System: Provide a twelve (12) year antifouling, underwater hull, and boot top coating system that complies with epoxy anticorrosive MIL-PRF-24647, Type I or II, and that complies with antifouling paint MIL-PRF-24647, Type II. Marking Compatibility: Provide preservation products that are suitable for use as hull and boot top markings on the ablative antifoulant paints. Substrate Compatibility: All preservation products must be compatible and have the ability to be applied over any existing coating on like surfaces. Statutory and Licensing Requirements Homeport Statute (10 U.S.C. 7299A): In accordance with the "Homeport Statute", this procurement will solicit offers only from offerors capable of performing the work in the Mayport homeport area. Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR): Offerors must have, or be able to obtain, an Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) or Government-approved equivalency by the time of contract award. Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP). Evaluation Method: Price-Only (Among conforming, responsible, and technically acceptable offerors�not a structured Part 15 LPTA). II. Summary of Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3) The successful contractor will be required to provide an express Marine Coatings Warranty (incorporated into FAR 52.212-4(o) Addendum) that includes: Two-Year Application Durability: Warranting that the paint is applied correctly so that it lasts a minimum of two (2) years after the date of application, and that the paint is usable up to its expiration date. Premature Failure Remedies: In the event of premature failure (e.g., delaminating, blistering, rust-through, softening, peeling), the Contractor shall furnish, at no cost to the Government, all materials and technical representative services necessary to recoat the failed area at any domestic or foreign location designated by the Government. Hull Scamping: Providing scamping of the underwater hull at no cost to the Government if more than twenty (20) percent of the underwater hull is heavily fouled due to poor performance of the antifouling within two (2) years of application. Misapplication Notice: The warranty is not voided by shipyard misapplication unless the Contractor's technical representative provides timely notice (written within 24 hours of verbal notice, and no later than 8 hours after the event) specifying the affected areas and required remedial actions. III. Questions for Industry The notice of interest should include a brief description of your company, its capabilities as they relate to the requirements, and answers to the following specific questions. Please limit your response to no more than five (5) pages (excluding certifications or licenses). Is your company a small or large business as defined by the Small Business Administration (SBA) under NAICS code 325510 (Paint and Coating Manufacturing)? If a small business, please specify your socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Women-Owned (WOSB), HUBZone, Veteran-Owned (VOSB), or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB)). How many employees does your company have? Does your company have an active website? If so, what is your company's website address? Does your company have a satisfactory performance record for this type of marine preservation work? Please provide examples of relevant and recent (within the last three years) past performance. Is your company able to provide both the desired paint product AND the manufacturer's guarantee/warranty without waiver or subcontracting, as detailed in the "Scope of Requirements" and "Navy Paint Warranty"? Given the complexity of the work described in this announcement, please describe your company's historical experience completing services on similar ship classes (e.g., Littoral Combat Ships or similar naval vessels) or briefly describe how your company is capable of meeting these requirements by the time of contract award. Given the complexity and size of the work described, does your company plan to submit a proposal/quote in response to the anticipated solicitation for the paint coatings and technical services of USS THE WICHITA (LCS 13)? IV. Submission Instructions Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive or Confidential to the responder, exempt from public release under the Freedom of Information Act. All information shall be provided free of charge to the Government. SERMC may request further information regarding the capabilities of respondents to meet the requirements set forth in the announcement. Where and When to Submit All proposals must be submitted electronically via email with the subject line: "USS WICHITA (LCS 13) Docked Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) - Paint OEM N4002726R0008". Submission Deadline: September 21, 2026, at 11:00 AM (1100 hours) SERMC Local Time. Submit to the following Points of Contact (POCs): sermc_c423.4_lcs_gold@us.navy.mil andres.m.walsh.civ@us.navy.mil anthony.r.turner14.civ@us.navy.mil jonathan.lebron.civ@us.navy.mil ***FULL DELIVERY OF MATERIALS ARE DUE TO THE DELIVERY ADDRESS IN JACKSONVILLE, FL LOCATED AT THE CONTRACTOR�S FACILITY WHERE THE SHIP WILL BE DRYDOCKED, 28 October 2026 ***PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: BAE SYSTEMS JACKSONVILLE SHIP REPAIR LLC, 8500 HECKSCHER DR, JACKSONVILLE FL 32226 Contracting Office Address: USS WICHITA (LCS 13) SERM-803-27 OEM Paint Southeast Regional Maintenance Center Building 1488, Naval Station Mayport Jacksonville, Florida 32228

title: Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) � Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, AL and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), TN
description: NOTICE OF INTENT-SOURCES SOUGHT The Defense Information Systems Agency /Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted to SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is for Army CONUS Enterprise (ACE) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) - Motorola Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support for Fort Novosel, Alabama, and Holston Army Ammunition Plant (HAAP), Tennessee. The period of performance is September 30, 2026, September 29, 2027, with one, one year option period. The requirement provides continued OEM extended warranty and associated maintenance support for Government-accepted Motorola LMR equipment and components covered by the applicable OEM warranty entitlement. Support includes OEM warranty administration; OEM technical support; diagnosis of covered equipment failures; repair or replacement of covered components; Return Material Authorization processing; warranty-related software and firmware updates made available under OEM entitlement; replacement components required to fulfill warranty obligations; applicable licensing; transportation and shipping associated with warranty actions; and coordination and tracking of warranty actions through closure. The contractor is required to provide OEM-backed technical and lifecycle support to ensure the continued operation of the existing Motorola LMR systems and maintain warranty coverage throughout the period of performance. At this time, the incumbent contractor Motorola Solutions, Inc.(Motorola) is the only source capable of fulfilling the requirement for OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the existing Motorola LMR systems and associated equipment. As the OEM, Motorola, possesses the proprietary technical data, system-specific knowledge, OEM repair capabilities, software and firmware support, replacement components, licensing, and warranty authority necessary to provide continued OEM-backed coverage for the installed Motorola equipment. Awarding this requirement to another source would not provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty coverage and could jeopardize the Government�s ability to maintain OEM-supported maintenance, compatibility, and lifecycle support for the existing Motorola LMR infrastructure and equipment. Such an outcome would introduce significant risks to mission-critical communications, operational readiness, and the security of Army Enterprise LMR systems. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 334210, Telephone Apparatus Manufacturing, will be used for determining company size status. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The Motorola OEM Extended Warranty and Maintenance Support requirement is currently being performed under the following contract: Contract Number: HC108424P0005 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Incumbent and Size: Motorola Solutions, Inc. � Large Business CAGE: 78205 Method of Previous Acquisition: Sole Source Period of Performance: July 31, 2024 through September 30, 2026 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall be the OEM, Motorola Solutions, Inc., or possess the necessary OEM authorization and capabilities to provide the required Motorola OEM extended warranty and maintenance support for the covered LMR systems and associated equipment in accordance with the PWS. Points of Contact: Contracting Officer: Melyssa D. Lafontaine, melyssa.d.lafontaine.civ@mail.mil Contract Specialist: Bobby J. Drees-Douglas, bobby.j.drees-douglas.civ@mail.mil

title: USCGC Stratton Shaft Alignment and Bearing Reaction Check
description: Statement of Work CGC Stratton Shaft Alignment and Bearing Reaction Check Intent: contractor must measure and report to USCG the Vertical and Horizontal Loads on the (2) bull gear bearings and (2) intermediate bearings, stern and strut bearings, using the Strain Gage Method. Period of Performance: 01 November 2026 � 01 January 2027 Location: USCGC Stratton, 42 Eagle Road Coast Guard Island, Alameda CA 94501 Contractor will install a total of (5) full bridge strain gage sets on the Port shaft, and (5) strain gage sets on the Starboard shaft, to complete the bearing load calculations. Contractor will also measure and report the vertical load on each line shaft bearing using the Hydraulic Jack/Load Cell method. Contractor will provide all specialty tools and calibrated instrumentation necessary to install the strain gages and measure the strain gage data. Contractor shall provide a final written report within 15 days after completion of the work covered by this scope of work. The report shall contain at a minimum the following: Introduction and References Project description Alignment calculations Alignment tests with strain gages Conclusions Recommendation for future action Data sheets on shaft model used to obtain reported results e.g. stations, strain gauge locations, diameters, lengths, load points, etc. Data sheets from Computer runs that computed reported results e.g. stations, deflections, stresses, bearing reactions, slopes, etc. References: Coast Guard Drawings Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 114-001, Rev B, Fairwaters and Rope Guard Installation Details & L/M (ASC114001) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 243-007, Rev E, Propulsion Shafting System Arrangement (ASC243008) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 243-008, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting and Appendage (ASC243001B) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-001, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting System Measured Bearing Reaction Report (ASC244001) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-002, Rev B, Stern Tube Seal & Strut Bearings Arrangement & Details & L/M (ASC244002) Coast Guard Drawing 750 WMSL 244-003, Rev -, Propulsion Shafting System Measured Bearing Reaction Report (AS2244001 Notes: For any references to be distributed, the contractor must be registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and provide your JCP number to the listed point of contact for this work. title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).
